messages:
sanjay: quick follow-up on the granule-based residency provenance prototype i ran this morning — short thread with results + open questions :eyes:

oleg: nice, what did you run?

sanjay: 24h canary across 4 hosts, mixed tenants. workload = sparse embeddings + small-batch chat. compared baseline per-page host-staging vs slot-granule hints (coarse per-segment hint emission). high level: median p50 +2.8ms, p95 +7.9ms, but host memory churn down ~42% and vram evict ops down ~37%.

maya: impressive drop in evicts. paste the flags you used?

sanjay: sure — minimal toggles on runtime image:

```
--residency.mode=granule-provenance
--granule.size=65536   # 64k
--residency.hint_window_ms=200
--evict.threshold=0.78
```

sanjay: also enabled demote-backpressure to avoid wholesale immediate reclaim during bursts.

harper: was this mixed prod traces or synthetic stress?

sanjay: mixed: 60% synthetic eviction spikes, 40% replayed prod traces (delayed long running requests + normal chat).

kyle: how is provenance stored? per-allocation metadata or side structure?

oleg: prototype keeps an 8-byte provenance tag per granule in a sidecar array (bitmap-like). avoids per-allocation lists and keeps hot-path reads cheap. overhead observed ~6% host memory.

maya: do small models regress? I worry coarse granules might blur tiny hotspots.

sanjay: yes — models with <8MB working set saw p95 regressions (~+12ms). we added a detector that falls back to per-page mode for small footprints.

tia: any concurrency safety issues for the tag updates during compaction?

oleg: we used CAS-based updates and one-way provenance transitions (cold->warm->hot). compaction explicitly clears tags for reclaimed granules. still need a formal audit of race windows.

sanjay: added telemetry: provenance histograms + compactness_ratio metric so ops can alert if coarsening creates harmful overlap.

infra-bot: deployment started on canary cluster ci-23 (image residency-proto:v2) — 2026-03-23T10:12:03Z

kyle: what's rollback if small-model regressions spike at scale?

sanjay: plan A: per-tenant detector — if compactness_ratio < 0.6 for 5m switch tenant to per-page. Plan B: global kill-switch from config service + less-aggressive model variant fallback.

harper: tenant-level switching across mixed nodes sounds risky. oscillation risk?

sanjay: we protect with hysteresis: need 2 consecutive 5m windows to flip and 15m cooldown before re-eval; also use a per-tenant leadership lease to avoid cross-node thrash.

oleg: tradeoff: 6% metadata overhead vs 37% fewer evicts. we should run unit-econ against GPU rental rates to justify the overhead.

maya: agreed — show me dollars saved per-tenant over sustained runs.

sanjay: i'll run a cost model next and post results here.

kyle: implementation note: we should standardize a small residency-hint API so compilers, routers, and batching can emit hints rather than ad-hoc signals.

sanjay: proto sketch: {granule_index, state_enum, source_enum, ttl_ms}. i'll attach in the RFC follow-up.

harper: include allowed transitions, GC semantics, and ops runbook (how to disable/diagnose) in that doc.

sanjay: next steps: run cost model, formal race audit for tag updates, finalize proto + RFC follow-up. tagging @oleg @maya @kyle for review :thumbsup:
